newsitem.title: SPAIN: Dutch premier sees EMU on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Dutch premier sees EMU on schedule.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Monday that Europe was on track for a timely launch of a single currency, but warned against any pre-selection of candidates for the monetary union.

Kok, whose country holds the revolving EU presidency, stressed the importance of sticking to the timetable and convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU). He was speaking at a conference in Madrid.
"The establishment of EMU is proceeding according to schedule," Kok said.

Kok met Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar late on Monday during a tour of Portugal, Spain and Italy to push plans for reform of the 15-nation European Union at a summit in Amsterdam next month. The meeting is aimed at preparing for incorporation of new members and Kok said he sees 20 or more nations in an expanded union.

"Enlargement of the union with central and eastern European countries is a political imperative," Kok said. Failed efforts to unify Europe in the past had dire consequences. With EMU, Kok said Europe will complete its internal market and strengthen its competitive position.
Regarding the Amsterdam summit, Kok said he hoped for reforms to strengthen the European parliament and European commission president.
Another aim is to reduce the requirements for unanimity in particular areas such as movement of persons and political and security policy.
In matters of justice and interior politics such as security, crime, drug trafficking and terrorism, Kok acknowledged that the Maastricht Treaty has disappointed.
